title: Melitzanes Yahni
subtitle: Greek aubergine stewed in tomato and olive oil
excerpt: Aubergine slowly stewed with onion, garlic, tinned tomatoes and plenty of olive oil until it becomes silky and rich. Eaten warm or at room temperature with crusty bread.
sourceNotes: Greek ladera tradition. Yahni refers to vegetables cooked slowly in oil and tomato without added stock.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze cooled portions for up to 2 months. Reheat gently on the hob with a splash of water.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles well in a larger pan. The cook time stays the same.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Tastes better the next day once the aubergine has fully absorbed the sauce.

content.text: Melitzanes yahni is a Greek olive oil stew. The aubergine collapses into the tomato sauce and turns deeply savoury. Eat it warm or let it cool to room temperature.
Salt the aubergine chunks and leave in a colander for 20 minutes. Rinse and pat dry with kitchen paper.
Warm the olive oil in a large saucepan over a medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 8 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and cook for 2 more minutes. Stir in the tomato puree and cook for 1 minute.
Add the aubergine chunks and stir to coat in the oil and onion mixture.
Pour in the tinned tomatoes. Add the oregano, salt and pepper. Stir well.
Cover and simmer on a low heat for 35 minutes. Stir every 10 minutes.
Remove the lid and cook for a further 10 minutes until the sauce is thick. Scatter over the parsley and serve.

items.symptom: The aubergine is still firm after the full cook time.
items.cause: The pieces were too large or the heat was too low.
items.fix: Cut smaller next time. Continue cooking with the lid on for another 10 to 15 minutes.

items.cause: The aubergine released a lot of liquid during cooking.
items.fix: Remove the lid and increase the heat to medium. Cook until the sauce reduces and thickens.

items.cause: The aubergine was not salted beforehand, or seasoning was light.
items.fix: Taste and add more salt. A little more olive oil drizzled over at the end deepens the flavour.
